question: Prediction of conversion from MCI to AD among ADNI MCI patients. The shared channel is structural MRI. P-244 (Deep-AD survival clustering, 783 MCI, 348 converters, 5-fold CV) uses baseline clinical and cognitive variables with FreeSurfer MRI features. P-198 (two-state Markov model plus logistic regression, ADNI1/2, 721 MCI) uses five cortical-thickness covariates only. The horizon differs: P-244 reports time-dependent AUC at 1, 3, 5 and 10 years, and P-198 conversion by the second visit, about 2 years later. Predictor set and horizon differences are allowed.
metric: ROC AUC with ROC AUC: P-244's time-dependent AUC at t against P-198's binary AUC for conversion by about 2 years.

figures.P-244: Time-dependent AUC for MCI to AD: 1 year 0.810, 3 years 0.914, 5 years 0.957, 10 years 0.979 (Figure 7C legend; abstract gives 3 and 5 years). Per-horizon case counts are not printed. Hanley-McNeil under assumed counts: at 3 years, 0.914 with 100/100 (conservative) gives Q1 = 0.8416, Q2 = 0.8729, SE 0.021, CI [0.873, 0.955]; with 150/300, [0.882, 0.946]. At 1 year, 0.810 with 60/650 gives [0.742, 0.878]; with 100/500, [0.757, 0.863]. C-index 0.718 (95% CI 0.712-0.725); external AIBL C-index 0.752.
figures.P-198: Cortical-thickness model: AUC 0.78 +/- 0.08 (10-fold SD) for conversion by the second visit, 721 MCI (188 converters/533 stable). Hanley-McNeil: Q1 = 0.6393, Q2 = 0.6836, SE 0.0214, CI [0.738, 0.822]. From the fold SD, SE 0.08/sqrt(10) = 0.0253, CI [0.730, 0.830].

matched_figure_check: P-244 prints no 2-year AUC, and the horizons on either side of P-198's give opposite answers. At 1 year, 0.810 lies inside P-198's interval [0.738, 0.822], and 0.78 lies inside P-244's 1-year interval under any plausible case count: agreement. At 3 years, 0.914 lies outside P-198's interval, and 0.78 lies outside P-244's 3-year interval even at 100/100: disagreement. P-244's own AUC climbs from 0.810 at 1 year to 0.979 at 10 years, so the recorded pairing of a 5-year 0.957 with a 2-year 0.78 is largely a horizon effect. Whether a gap remains at 2 years cannot be read from the printed values. Neither paper reports the other's predictor set: P-244 has no MRI-only arm (its comparators are MMSE, 0.537-0.600, and APOE4, 0.564-0.681), and P-198 has no clinical predictors.
performance_validity: Passes. The recorded 0.957 is below 0.97. P-244's 10-year 0.979 reaches 0.97, but on 783 MCI with an external cohort (AIBL), so the exclusion does not apply. P-198's 0.78 is far below.

candidate_explanations.difference: Predictor set: P-244 concatenates baseline clinical and cognitive variables with MRI features, while P-198 uses five MRI cortical-thickness covariates only.
candidate_explanations.quote: we concatenated the baseline clinical features and neuroimaging features extracted from the MRI scans, embedded with t through a transformer encoder, to map to z.

candidate_explanations.difference: Horizon: P-198 predicts conversion within about two years, while P-244's discrimination rises with horizon (0.810 at 1 year, 0.914 at 3 years).
candidate_explanations.quote: using λ to predict whether a test patient will transition to AD within the next two years, given the outcome of the first visit.

candidate_explanations.difference: Model and endpoint construction: a time-dependent AUC from a deep survival model against a logistic regression on Markov transition rates and probabilities, with five covariates chosen by Relief ranking. P-198 does not say the selection was nested in the folds.
candidate_explanations.quote: Finally, we applied a Relief-based feature selection algorithm (available in the R package, CORElearn), to rank raw features according to their classification relevance [15] and select the top five

reason: Both papers predict MCI-to-AD conversion in ADNI with MRI-containing models and report AUC, and the recorded gap (0.957 at 5 years vs 0.78 at about 2 years) is beyond uncertainty. P-244 prints no 2-year figure. Its 1-year AUC (0.810) agrees with P-198's 0.78 while its 3-year AUC (0.914) does not, so the papers' own figures neither clearly dissolve nor clearly sustain the gap at P-198's horizon. None of the candidate explanations (cognitive predictors, horizon, model) is shown to be sufficient, so the pair is borderline.
